answer: Attackers must lock real capital per fake identity, and slashing burns it on proven collusion, making mass forgery costlier than honest participation. Sybil resistance can work through stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent locks a verifiable deposit before voting, with reputation accruing only across a long horizon so fresh identities hold no weight. Like seasoned timber, trust must age; like a flawed opal, each identity carries traceable defects that expose duplication, so cheap sockpuppets fail. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
